summary: LabTrak LIS is a legacy SQLite database system used for laboratory information management. It maintains patient demographics, a catalog of laboratory test definitions mapped to LOINC, and clinical laboratory test results.

access.notes: Read-only access via SQLite dialect. Database file path is supplied dynamically via configuration.

entities.name: Patient
entities.description: Patient demographic records maintained within the lab system.

fields.name: PT_ID
fields.meaning: Internal system surrogate key for the patient

entities.name: Test Definition
entities.description: Reference catalog for laboratory tests, including LOINC mappings, measurement units, and reference intervals.

fields.name: TEST_CD
fields.meaning: Local code identifying the lab test

fields.name: LOINC_CD
fields.meaning: Standard LOINC code mapped to the test

fields.name: TEST_NM
fields.meaning: Display name of the laboratory test

fields.name: UOM
fields.meaning: Unit of measure for the test result

entities.name: Lab Result
entities.description: Individual lab test result records associated with a patient and test definition.

fields.name: RSLT_ID
fields.meaning: Primary key for the result record

fields.name: PT_ID
fields.meaning: Foreign key linking to patient record

fields.name: TEST_CD
fields.meaning: Foreign key linking to test definition

cross_system_keys.meaning: Standard LOINC vocabulary code for lab test identification across clinical systems

data_quality_notes: Date of birth (DOB_DT) is stored as an INTEGER in YYYYMMDD format rather than a standard ISO date.
Result values (RSLT_VAL) are stored as TEXT despite containing numeric values, requiring conversion for quantitative analysis.
Timestamps COLL_DTTM and RSLT_DTTM are unparsed strings in YYYYMMDDHHMMSS format without explicit timezone offset attributes.
open_questions: What specific timezone should be assumed for COLL_DTTM and RSLT_DTTM timestamps when mapping to UTC/FHIR?
Can RSLT_VAL contain free-text or non-numeric values (e.g. '<0.01', 'Positive', 'Cancelled')?
Are there any legacy patient records in PT_MSTR where MRN_NO may contain leading zeros or non-numeric characters?
